asides.chased: {names} were fetched in on the bells.

title: Elected in {riding}
Election night in {riding}
text: {riding} came in by {votes} votes after a count that took most of the night. {rival} conceded before you'd thought of what to say, and {gov} formed a {govKind} government without needing to know your name.
You won {riding} by {votes} votes. The broadcaster had called a {govKind} {gov} government before your own race was settled, so your victory party watched someone else's on television first.

title: Sworn in for {riding}
The member for {riding}
text: The Clerk read the oath, you read it back, and {riding} had a member in the {nth} Parliament. Nobody had learned your name yet.
You took the oath for {riding} on the first day of the {nth} Parliament, one of a class of new members the whip's office was already sorting into piles.

title: {title}
text: {blurb}

title: The first call from the whip's office
text: {whip} wanted you on {bill}, and you gave your word before you'd finished your coffee. It was the first time the whip leaned on you. It would not be the last.
The whip's office called about {bill}. {whip} did the talking and you did the agreeing, and you walked out a reliable vote and felt it.

title: You said no to the whip
The first call from the whip's office
text: {whip} called you in about {bill} and you told them no. They wrote something down. It was the first time the whip leaned on you, and the first time you leaned back.
The whip's office wanted your vote on {bill}. You heard {whip} out and kept it. Nobody shouted, which was worse.

title: The call you didn't take
text: The whip's office called about {bill} and you didn't go. {whip} noticed. In that building, not going is an answer.

title: The first time you broke the line
Against the line
text: {bill} was whipped {line}, and you stood with the {vote}s. The walk to your feet was longer than it looked from the gallery.
Your first rebellion: {bill}, whipped {line}, and you voted {vote}. The whip's office keeps a file on every member. Yours got its first page.

title: Carried {by}
Confidence, carried {by}
The government held, {by}
text: {bill} was a matter of confidence and it carried {by}, {yeas} to {nays}. Your benches thumped their desks as if it had never been in doubt.
The House divided {yeas} to {nays} on {bill}, and the government lived another week. It carried {by}, and you had counted every one of them.
Confidence, {yeas} to {nays}, on {bill}. It carried {by}, which on the Hill is a comfortable night and in the whip's office is a warning.

title: {short}
The government fell, {short}
Lost, {short}
text: {bill} was confidence, and the government lost it {yeas} to {nays}. {Short}. The Speaker read the numbers and the House went quiet, then loud.
The count on {bill} was {yeas} to {nays}: {short}. By evening the word election was being said out loud.
{bill} went down {yeas} to {nays}, {short}. You had the names in your notebook before the Clerk had finished reading them.

title: Brought them down {by}
The government fell {by}
text: {bill} went against the government {yeas} to {nays}. They fell {by}, and your benches were on their feet before the Speaker had finished.
The government lost the confidence of the House on {bill}, {yeas} to {nays}. The margin was {margin}, and it was enough. Somebody on your side had a bottle in a desk.

title: {short} of bringing them down
The government held, {by}
text: You went after the government on {bill} and lost, {yeas} to {nays}, {short}. The other side cheered as if they'd meant it all along.
{bill} was confidence and the government held, {yeas} to {nays}. {Short} of an election. You went back over the names on the walk home.

title: A tie, and the Speaker's vote
text: {bill} tied, {yeas} to {nays}. The Speaker cast the deciding vote the way Speakers do, to let the House decide another day, and the government lived on a technicality.

title: A tie, and the Speaker's vote
text: {bill} tied, {yeas} to {nays}, and the Speaker's casting vote went against it. The government fell on a single vote that wasn't even a member's.

title: Your name on a bill
The private member's bill
text: Your name came up in the private members' lottery and you put it on {bill}. A backbencher's bill rarely passes. It gets you into rooms you weren't in before.
The lottery gave you a slot and you spent it on {bill}. The whip asked who had written it. You had.

title: {bill} passed
Your bill passed
text: {bill} passed second reading {by}. Your name is on something now, and it will be on it after you've gone.
Your bill, {bill}, carried {by} at second reading. You read the division list twice to be sure of it.

title: {bill} defeated
Your bill went down
text: {bill} was defeated at second reading. You know who voted for it, and so does the whip.
Your bill, {bill}, died at second reading. The members who'd said 'of course' in the lobby said nothing in the division.

title: Noticed: reliable
text: The whip's office had you down as reliable. It is the nicest thing they say about anyone, and they mean it as a job description.

title: Noticed: useful trouble
text: The whip's office had you down as useful trouble: someone who rebels on the right things, and can be talked to about the rest.

title: Assistant whip
text: {whip} had two names for the chair and picked yours. {rival} congratulated you in the lobby with the face of someone already counting to the next vacancy.
The chair in the whip's office was yours, and with it a row of members to answer for. {rival} took it well, in public.

title: Passed over for the chair
text: The chair in the whip's office went to {rival}. 'Next time,' {whip} said, which is what whips say.
{whip} gave the chair to {rival}. You found out from the seating chart.

title: A committee of your own
text: You took a committee chair instead: a title, a staff, a gavel of your own, and your name still on the whip's list.

title: Leaning on a friend
text: You needed {friend} on {bill} and you didn't ask nicely. They voted the line. They haven't forgotten how you asked.

title: Asking a friend
text: You asked {friend} to vote the line on {bill} as a friend, not as a whip. It is a different thing, and you both knew it.

title: Letting a friend go
text: {friend}'s riding hated {bill}, and you let them vote it. The deputy whip found the gap in your row and asked you about it.

title: Deputy whip
text: Your row carried, week after week, and the deputy's desk was yours. The count was yours now, and so was being wrong about it.
{whip} put your name forward and the deputy's chair came with a key to the count. Your phone started ringing at eleven at night.

title: Back to the backbench
text: The whip's office decided you were too soft for a row. You went back to the backbench with a reputation for kindness, which in that building is a diagnosis.

title: Back to the backbench
text: Your row stopped answering your calls. The whip's office decided that was your doing and sent you back to the backbench.

title: Off the deputy's desk
text: You called votes safe that weren't, more than once. The deputy's desk went to someone who counted better, and you went back to a row.

title: Out of the whip's office
text: The caucus had had enough, and {leader} agreed with the caucus. The whip's office went to someone else on a Friday afternoon.

title: Back to the backbench
text: The government fell on your count. You stayed in the House, on the backbench, which is where whips who lose confidence votes go.

title: Back to the backbench
text: The caucus turned you out of the whip's office, and you stayed to sit among them on the backbench. Some of them still can't look at you.

title: You said no to the leader
text: {leader} offered you a way out of the whip's office and into something better paid. You said no. They said they understood, which is not the same thing as agreeing.

title: Chief Whip
text: {chief} went to cabinet and {leader} gave you the chair. The whole caucus is your row now.
{leader} made you Chief Whip the week {chief} went to cabinet. The office has a better window and no door that stays shut.

title: The chair went elsewhere
text: {chief} went to cabinet and {other} got the Chief Whip's chair. You were still the deputy, which is a job and not a consolation.

title: You turned down {portfolio}
text: {leader} offered you {portfolio}. You turned it down to stay in the whip's office. The offer, they said, stands. Offers say that.
{leader} had {portfolio} for you, with a driver. You said the whip's office still needed you, and meant it, mostly.

title: You showed up for {first}
There for {first}
text: When {name} {what}, you went. It cost you an evening you didn't have, and {first} hasn't forgotten it.
{name} {what}, and you made the time. It is the kind of thing nobody puts in the record, which is why it's here.
You cleared an evening when {name} {what}. Nobody asked you to. {first} noticed that most of all.

title: You didn't go
The evening you didn't spend
text: When {name} {what}, you had your own week. They noticed you didn't come by.
{name} {what}, and you let it pass. You meant to call. You didn't call.

title: Your word, broken
text: You'd promised {name} your vote and you didn't give it. Their friends heard about it before you'd left the chamber. It was the first time, and it's the one you remember.

title: Your first question
text: Your first question in Question Period went to {minister}, on {topic}, and it was a soft one. Your benches thumped their desks anyway. It was a start.

title: Your first question
text: You put your first question to {minister} on {topic}. They had the answer ready, and the gallery moved on to someone else.

title: Your first question landed
text: Your first question in Question Period landed. {minister} had nothing ready on {topic}, and the press gallery wrote it down.

title: Your first question, for home
text: You went off the script for your first question and asked {minister} about {topic}. {riding} heard about it by supper.

title: Re-elected in {riding}
Back for the {nth} Parliament
{riding} again
text: {riding} sent you back to the {nth} Parliament.
The campaign was five weeks of church basements and the count was over by eleven. You held {riding} for the {nth} Parliament.
You held {riding}. The returning officer said your name for the {nth} Parliament like they'd got used to it.

title: Lost {riding}
text: {riding} went the other way. You thanked the volunteers at midnight, and then you went home, and the House went on without you.

title: Deselected
text: The riding association in {riding} chose someone else before the writ dropped. You learned it from a phone call, which is how it is always learned.

title: Across the floor
text: You crossed the floor from {from} to {to}. It is a short walk. You start again as a rookie, with your name going ahead of you.
You left {from} for {to}, carrying your files across the aisle in a box. Your old benches watched you sit down.

title: The room turned
text: The caucus came for {leader} and got them. {newLeader} has the leader's office now.

title: The room held
text: {ringleader}'s list came up short, and {leader} kept the party. For now, everyone said, though not in the room.

title: The room turned on you
text: {ringleader} had the names, and the caucus took the whip's office from you in a single morning.

title: The room held for you
text: {ringleader} came for the whip's office with a list, and the caucus wouldn't sign it. You kept your job and learned who'd been asked.

title: You stood down
text: You stood down from {riding}. The whip's office sent a card, signed by people you had once threatened, and they meant every word.

title: Cabinet: {portfolio}
text: {leader} gave you {portfolio}, and you left the whip's office for a ministry. The new whip has your files. Some of them are about you.

title: Out of the whip's office
text: You took the leader's offer and left the whip's office: better hours, better pay, and nobody calling at eleven to ask where you are.

title: Resigned
text: The government fell on your count, and you resigned the whip's office the next morning. The letter was two lines. You wrote eleven drafts.

title: Overthrown
text: The caucus turned on you, and you took the hint, and then the door.
